title: Care and Maintenance of Fabrics

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four statements or pairs of ½ mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or arrange in sequence).

questions.q: Match the stain with the removing agent: (A) Henna (B) Blood (C) Old coffee (D) Nail polish; (i) Borax (ii) Methylated spirit (iii) Warm milk (iv) Diluted ammonia.
Arrange the activities in the correct sequence to launder clothes and save time and energy: (A) Rinse the clothes (B) Starch the clothes (C) Remove stains (D) Soak clothes.
questions.answer: (C) Remove stains; (D) Soak clothes; (A) Rinse the clothes; (B) Starch the clothes.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) Shoe polish and lipstick make the fabric feel ______. (ii) Diluted ammonia with cold water is used to remove ______ stains. (iii) Wool is washed by ______ method. (iv) Polyester should be ironed at ______ degrees C.
questions.answer: (i) slippery. (ii) blood (animal or protein) stains. (iii) kneading and squeezing. (iv) 150.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Only white-coloured clothes should be soaked. (ii) Soak very dirty clothes separately. (iii) Too many clothes should not be soaked together. (iv) Cotton clothes are starched to give them whiteness.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) True. (iii) True. (iv) False – starch gives a smooth, crisp and fresh look; whiteness comes from blue or brighteners.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Bacteria can grow on damp clothes. (ii) Cotton clothes should be hung on a clothesline. (iii) Clothes should be rinsed at least three times to remove soapy water. (iv) Old ink stains can be removed by using sour milk (buttermilk).
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) True. (iii) True. (iv) True.
questions.note: October 2025 had 'at least two times' in item (iii); the textbook says at least three times, or till the water is clear.

questions.q: Rearrange the correct sequence of starching clothes: (a) Wring excess water and dry in sun (b) Wet the shirt (c) Dissolve starch in water (d) Dip shirt in starch water and stir.
questions.answer: (c) Dissolve starch in water; (b) wet the shirt; (d) dip the shirt in the starch water; (a) wring out and dry in the sun.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Laundering is the same as washing. (ii) Airing of clothes helps when they are not to be washed at once. (iii) Stains should be removed before washing. (iv) Synthetics should be squeezed well before drying.
questions.answer: (i) False – it includes washing or dry cleaning, finishing and storing. (ii) True. (iii) True. (iv) False – squeezing makes them wrinkle; dry on a hanger.

questions.q: Match the fabric with the care: (i) Silk (ii) Wool (iii) Coloured cotton (iv) White cotton; (a) dry flat on a paper outline (b) neutral soap and gum arabic (c) no soaking and dry in shade (d) soak in warm water and blue.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Which four precautions should be adopted while laundering cotton clothes (or removing stains)? Give the first four.
questions.answer: Sort the clothes by colour and dirt; mend tears first; soak only white cottons for not more than half an hour and very dirty ones separately; rinse at least three times; dry in the sun (coloured ones in shade) and store only when completely dry.

questions.q: Write any two bases by which you can identify stains. Give two examples of each.
questions.answer: By colour – curry is yellow, tea or coffee is brown, grass is green. By smell – egg, paint, shoe polish have their own smell. By feel – paint or sugar makes the fabric hard and stiff, lipstick or shoe polish makes it slippery (any two bases).

questions.q: Write any four precautions you will adopt while washing woollens at home.
questions.answer: Draw an outline of the knitted garment on paper; use mild alkaline detergent in lukewarm water; wash by kneading and squeezing, no rubbing or wringing; rinse thoroughly; dry flat in the shade on the outline; store dry with naphthalene balls.

questions.q: List four steps involved in the process of laundering clothes.
questions.answer: Soaking, washing, rinsing, finishing (starching or blueing), drying, ironing and storing (any four).

questions.q: Mention four damages that can occur if clothes are not laundered in time.
questions.answer: Bacteria and fungus grow causing skin problems; clothes smell; the fabric loses strength; stains set and become permanent; clothes look dirty and unattractive.

questions.q: Briefly explain the process of laundering a cotton shirt at home.
questions.answer: Mend and sort the shirt; remove stains; soak white shirt in warm soapy water for up to half an hour; wash collar and cuffs with hand friction and the rest by kneading; rinse three times; apply blue and starch; dry in the sun; iron when evenly damp with a hot iron; store when completely dry.

questions.q: Why should stains be removed before washing?
questions.answer: Some stains become permanent when exposed to the chemicals in soap or detergent, hot water and ironing, and old stains need much more effort and give poor results.

questions.q: Distinguish between washing and dry cleaning.
questions.answer: Washing removes dirt with soap or detergent and water and suits colourfast fabrics; dry cleaning removes dirt with grease absorbents and solvents and is used for leather, fur, selected silks and woollens, zari and costly fabrics.

questions.q: How much starch and water are needed to starch 4–5 clothes? How can the stiffness be varied?
questions.answer: Two tablespoons of starch in 5 litres of water are enough for 4–5 clothes. For very stiff fabric dilute the full-strength starch with 2–3 times water; add 4–6 times water for reasonably good stiffness.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Why do you wash cotton clothes in soapy water, rinse and starch them? Write the steps of laundering white cotton clothes (any six).
questions.answer: (1) Sort and mend. (2) Remove stains. (3) Soak white cottons in warm water for up to half an hour. (4) Wash in soap solution – light clothes by kneading, heavy ones with a stick, very dirty parts with hand or brush. (5) Rinse at least three times and add blue. (6) Starch for a smooth, fresh look and dry in the sun; iron when damp; store when completely dry.

questions.q: Describe the technique of sponging to remove a stain.
questions.answer: Place an absorbent paper or cloth (blotter) under the stain so that the right side of the stain faces it; sponge on the wrong side with a soft cloth dipped in the stain remover; rub gently from the outer edge towards the centre with light circular strokes so that the stain does not spread; change the blotter as soon as it shows the stain; rinse well afterwards.

questions.q: Suggest the correct procedure for washing a brightly printed silk scarf.
questions.answer: Do not soak; use lukewarm or cold water and a good neutral soap with light pressure; rinse well in cold water; apply gum arabic and dry in the shade; iron with a warm iron when evenly damp (silk stains if water is sprinkled on dry cloth); store on a hanger when completely dry.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Which five precautions should be adopted while laundering cotton clothes?
questions.answer: (1) Sort white and coloured clothes; read labels; mend tears first. (2) Remove stains before washing. (3) Soak only white cottons in warm water for not more than half an hour, very dirty clothes separately, not too many together. (4) Wash by hand friction, brush or stick as required and rinse at least three times. (5) Use blue and starch (not on undergarments); dry white clothes in the sun and coloured ones inside out in shade; iron when damp and store only when completely dry.

questions.q: Which five precautions should be adopted while removing stains from clothes (delicate garments)?
questions.answer: (1) Remove the stain while it is fresh. (2) Identify the stain by colour, smell and feel and choose the right agent. (3) Try the chemical on a hidden portion first. (4) Use dilute and mild reagents. (5) Sponge on the wrong side with a blotter underneath, from outer edge inward, or dip. (6) Avoid heat on protein stains. (7) Rinse several times so the chemical does not damage the fabric.

or.q: Mahima ruined her coloured synthetic clothes after washing them at home. What five possible mistakes may she have committed?
or.answer: She may have soaked coloured clothes; used hot water, which makes synthetics wrinkle or melt; used strong detergent or rubbed hard; squeezed them tightly; dried them in strong sun instead of shade; or used a hot iron.

questions.q: Reena spoiled her white cotton clothes while removing stains. What could be five possible reasons?
questions.answer: She may not have identified the stain and used the wrong agent; used a strong reagent that damaged the fabric; used heat on a protein stain so it set; let the stain become old before treating it; did not rinse the chemical out properly; or ironed before the stain was removed.
